Autumn of Yuanchu 2 (115): Liaodong Xianbei surrounded Wulu (Liaodong commandery); Han cleared the countryside and denied them booty.
元初二年秋 is the autumn of the second Yuanchu year; "Yuanchu 115" fuses the era with the Western year.
Year six autumn: ten thousand Dai riders burst inward, torched offices, slew magistrates, and vanished.
Year five, autumn: ten thousand Dai riders burst inward, torched offices, slew magistrates, and vanished.
五年秋 is the autumn of the fifth (Yuanchu) year, not the sixth.
Yongning 120: Wulun and Qizhijian of Liaoxi presented Deng Zun their surrender and gifts.
Yongning 1 (120): Wulun and Qizhijian of Liaoxi presented Deng Zun their surrender and gifts.
永寧元年 is the first Yongning year (120 CE); "Yongning 120" fuses the era with the Western year.
Next spring Chief Commander Zhang Guo led Southern Xiongnu infantry and cavalry over ten thousand beyond the wall, routed them, and captured more than two thousand loads of baggage.

Next spring Chief Commander Zhang Guo sent an aide leading the Southern Chanyu’s infantry and cavalry over ten thousand beyond the wall, routed them, and captured more than two thousand loads of baggage.
遣從事將南單于兵 means Zhang Guo sent an aide to lead the Southern Chanyu’s troops; he did not lead them himself.
Yangjia 132 winter: Rong Zhuwei’s raid yielded heavy trophies; emperor promoted Zhu Gui’s party with silk bales.
Winter of Yangjia 1 (132): Geng Ye sent Rong Zhuwei with Zhu Gui and other Wuhuan chiefs on a raid that yielded heavy trophies; the emperor promoted Zhu Gui’s party with graded silks.
陽嘉元年冬 is Yangjia 1 (132), not "Yangjia 132"; the idiomatic line also drops that Geng Ye (耿曄) dispatched the raid.
Kin hid the boy and named him Tanshi Huai.
His mother secretly had her family raise the boy and named him Tanshi Huai.
妻私語家令收養焉: the wife secretly told her family to take him in and raise him; the idiomatic "Kin hid the boy" drops the mother’s agency.
A rival chief rustled his uncle’s herd; Huai charged solo, scattered them, won every beast back, and earned universal dread.
A rival chief rustled his maternal family’s herd; Huai charged solo, scattered them, won every beast back, and earned universal dread.
外家 means his mother’s family (maternal kin), not specifically an uncle.
Yongshou 156 autumn: Huai struck Yunzhong with a few thousand riders.
Autumn of Yongshou 2 (156): Huai struck Yunzhong with a few thousand riders.
永壽二年秋 is the autumn of the second Yongshou year; "Yongshou 156" fuses era and Western year.
Yanxi 158 opened with Xianbei strikes along the northern frontier.
Yanxi 1 (158) opened with Xianbei strikes along the northern frontier.
延熹元年 is the first Yanxi year (158); "Yanxi 158" fuses era and Western year.
Yanxi 166 summer: wave riders tore through nine border prefectures until Zhang Huan chased them back across the frontier.
Summer of Yanxi 9 (166): wave riders tore through nine border prefectures until Zhang Huan chased them back across the frontier.
九年夏 is the summer of the ninth Yanxi year (166); "Yanxi 166" fuses era and Western year.
Xiping 174 winter: Xia Yu’s Tuge riders chased Xianbei out of Beidi commandery.
Winter of Xiping 3 (174): Xia Yu’s Tuge riders chased Xianbei out of Beidi commandery.
熹平三年冬 is the winter of the third Xiping year (174); "Xiping 174" fuses era and Western year.
Note three: campaigning against alien peoples has honored precedent since antiquity.
Campaigning against alien peoples has honored precedent since antiquity.
The Chinese 征討殊類，所由尚矣 has no note marker here; "Note three:" is spurious in the literal line.
He sent Huo Qubing to strike the Xiongnu, enfeoffing him on Mount Langjuxu and bringing him to overlook the Hanhai.
He sent Huo Qubing to strike the Xiongnu, and he performed the feng sacrifice on Mount Langjuxu and ascended to overlook the Hanhai.
封狼居胥山 means Huo Qubing performed the feng sacrifice on Mount Langjuxu, not that he was enfeoffed there; 登臨瀚海 describes his own ascent.
State monopolies note one riveted smugglers’ ankles.
Note one: Emperor Wu put Dongguo Xianyang and others in charge of the empire’s salt and iron; anyone daring to cast coins or sell salt privately had his left foot fettered.
The idiomatic line drops Emperor Wu (武帝) and Dongguo Xianyang (東郭咸陽) and the offenses punished.
Bandits note two cut communications through Taishan in 99 BCE.
Note two: in Tianhan 2 (99 BCE) under Emperor Wu, Xu Bo and other bandits of Taishan and Langye held the mountains, attacked towns, and cut the roads.
The idiomatic line drops Emperor Wu, the era Tianhan 2, Langye, and the bandit leader Xu Bo (徐勃).
Straight-arrow commissioners note three carried axe authority district by district.
Note three: Emperor Wu sent Straight-Pointing Envoys such as Bao Shengzhi, in embroidered robes and bearing axes, to pursue and arrest bandits district by district.
The idiomatic line drops Emperor Wu and the named envoy Bao Shengzhi (暴勝之).
Xia Yu and Tian Yan are hardly superior generals, while Xianbei strength matches earlier highs.
Xia Yu and Tian Yan are not necessarily abler than Duan Jiong, while Xianbei strength matches earlier highs.
未必過熲 compares Yu and Yan specifically with Duan Jiong (熲); the idiomatic line drops the comparison.
When Zhuya commandery rebelled, Emperor Yuan accepted Jia Juan's counsel and issued an edict: "Zhuya turned rebel; advisers split between conquer or abandon.
When Zhuya commandery rebelled, Emperor Yuan accepted Jia Juanzhi's counsel and issued an edict: "Zhuya turned rebel; advisers split between conquer or abandon.
賈捐之 is Jia Juanzhi; "Jia Juan" truncates the given name.
When Zhuya commandery rebelled Emperor Yuan accepted Jia Juan’s counsel and issued an edict: “Zhuya turned rebel; advisers split between conquer or abandon.
When Zhuya commandery rebelled Emperor Yuan accepted Jia Juanzhi’s counsel and issued an edict: “Zhuya turned rebel; advisers split between conquer or abandon.
賈捐之 is Jia Juanzhi; "Jia Juan" truncates the given name.
Li Mu held Zhao’s north commentary three.
Commentary three: the Records says Li Mu was a fine general of Zhao’s northern frontier.
史記曰，李牧，趙之北邊良將也: the idiomatic "Li Mu held Zhao’s north commentary three" misplaces the note marker and drops the source and the judgment 良將.
Minor Qianman yielded rule to uncle Kuitou.
Helian’s son Qianman was still young, so Kuitou, son of Helian’s elder brother, took the throne.
兄子魁頭立: Kuitou was the son of Helian’s elder brother (Qianman’s cousin), not his uncle, and it was Helian’s succession he took, not something Qianman yielded.
The imperial diary lists all three peoples without repetition.
The Basic Annals record that in the sixth month of that year the Southern Xiongnu, together with the Wuhuan and Xianbei, raided nine frontier commanderies.
The idiomatic line does not translate the Chinese; 本紀是年六月南匈奴及烏桓、鮮卑寇緣邊九郡 records a joint raid on nine frontier commanderies.
